entries.title: 3D
entries.summary: 180° Y-axis rotation. Requires CSS: backface-visibility: hidden; transform-style: preserve-3d; on both scene-inners. Parent needs perspective: 1200px.

entries.title: Blur
entries.summary: All blur transitions scale with energy. See SKILL.md "Blur Intensity by Energy" for the full table.

entries.title: Cover
entries.summary: Full-screen (1920x1080) colored divs slide across staggered. Scene swaps while covered.

entries.title: Destruction
entries.summary: The outgoing scene literally burns away from a corner. A fire front expands with noise-based irregular edges, a canvas draws the scorched char line at the burn boundary, and individual text characters/elements chip off and fall with gravity as the fire reaches them. The incoming scene reveals behind the burn.

entries.title: Dissolve
entries.summary: Simple opacity swap. The baseline.

entries.title: Distortion
entries.summary: RGB-tinted overlays (NOT multiply blend — use normal blending at 35% opacity) jitter with large offsets. Scene itself also jitters.

entries.title: Grid
entries.summary: Grid of colored cells covers the frame in a ripple from center. Scene swaps at 50% coverage. Cells fade out in ripple.

entries.title: Light
entries.summary: Multiple warm-colored overlays wash across frame. Needs: a flat warm tint layer + 2-3 bright radial gradient divs, all larger than the frame so edges are never visible.

entries.title: Mechanical
entries.summary: Two full-screen halves close from top and bottom, meet in the middle. Swap while closed. Open again.

entries.title: Other
entries.summary: Old scene falls down with slight rotation. New scene was behind it. Needs z-index.

entries.title: Linear / Push
entries.summary: Both scenes move together — new pushes old out.

entries.title: Radial / Shape
entries.summary: Expanding circle from center reveals new scene.

entries.title: Scale / Zoom
entries.summary: Old zooms past camera + blurs, new zooms in from behind.

entries.title: Broadcast-realism aspect + palette
entries.summary: For "caught on TV" trend recreations, 1:1 square reads more real than strict 9:16 — real broadcast cameras shoot 16:9, so a tall portrait crop triggers the AI-detector eye. Plus a cross-cutting default toward natural / muted color over neon.
